name: model-coverage-3d
title: Model Coverage 3D — AS/Organ Coverage from BioModel-DO Annotations
question:
Of the HRA ASCT+B-3D crosswalk's 1,400+ anatomical structures (and ~81
reference organs), which are covered by a mechanistic model — and can
that coverage be viewed directly on the 3D anatomy?

study_card.goal: Cross the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk's anatomical structures with the biomodel-DO organ->models index, at organ granularity, and confirm the composite loads a non-empty per-AS coverage list plus summary counts.
study_card.mechanism: CoverageStep.update -> build_coverage(query, max_results) = build_biomodel_do_catalog(...) x fetch_crosswalk(...) -> per-AS `covered` flag (own Uberon has models, or its organ_glb belongs to a covered organ) -> coverage + coverage_summary -> RAMEmitter.
study_card.expected_result: A non-empty coverage list where at least one anatomical structure/organ is covered by the glucose-regulation biomodel-DO set (pancreas/kidney/liver expected to dominate).
study_card.main_expert_question: Is organ-granularity coverage (propagating from a reference organ's Uberon to every AS node cut from its GLB) a meaningful enough proxy for 'this anatomy is modeled', or does it overstate coverage for fine-grained AS nodes with no direct model evidence?

biological_summary:
Glucose regulation is a whole-body, multi-organ circuit: the liver
buffers glucose via glycogen synthesis/breakdown, the pancreatic islets
set the hormonal signal (insulin/glucagon) that drives that buffering,
and the kidney contributes via gluconeogenesis and glucose reabsorption.
A BioModels search for "glucose regulation" surfaces the mechanistic
models literature has built for this circuit, and this study asks how
much of the HRA's fine-grained 3D anatomy those models actually touch
once their organ annotations are crossed with the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk —
the query-scoped companion to `corpus-coverage`'s full-catalog sweep.
readouts: per-AS covered flag + n_models/model_ids in the coverage list

report.title: Model Coverage 3D — glucose-regulation query covers liver + pancreas only
report.objective:
Of the HRA ASCT+B-3D crosswalk's anatomical structures, which are
covered by the glucose-regulation BioModels search set (25 results),
and can that coverage be viewed on the 3D anatomy?
report.conclusion:
Crossing the 25-result "glucose regulation" biomodel-DO catalog against
the 1,730-Uberon-row crosswalk marks 58/1,730 AS nodes covered (3.4%),
all propagating from 4 of 114 source-organ GLBs: `VH_F_Liver`,
`VH_M_Liver`, `VH_F_Pancreas`, `VH_M_Pancreas` (both sexes of liver and
pancreas). No kidney coverage at this query scope — organ-granularity
coverage is exactly as broad as the underlying BioModels search/organ
annotation, confirming the propagation rule fires correctly (liver and
pancreas AS nodes light up, nothing else does) rather than overstating
coverage.
report.caveat:
Coverage here is bounded by the 25-result query scope, not model
availability — the full 1,096-model corpus covers far more (see
`corpus-coverage`: 635/1,730 AS nodes, 31/114 organs, including
kidney). Organ-granularity propagation also still overstates
fine-grained coverage: a covered organ's Uberon marks every AS node
cut from its GLB, not just nodes with direct model evidence.
NOTE: the embedded 3D viewer packs under this study's `viz/hra/` are
rendered from the FULL-CORPUS coverage (635/1,730, kidney included),
NOT this study's glucose-query baseline — so the 3D organs show more
green than the 58/1,730 figure above. See the `corpus-coverage` study
for the matching corpus report.
